newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle slow before holiday- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle slow before holiday- feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Tuesday were seen slow as the industry winds down for the New Year's holiday on Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
Activity was extremely slow on Monday, with only a handful of cattle reported sold, they said.
About 100 select and choice heifers in Kansas sold at $66.00 per cwt, according to USDA and private sources.
Packer bids ranged from $65.00 to $66.00, with asking levels at $67.00 to mostly $68.00, they said.
Strong demand following the holiday could push prices up $1.00 to $67.00, the feedlot sources said.
Further strength could result from reaction to lower CBOT corn futures on Monday and sharply higher CME pork complex futures, the market sources said.

Pork futures rallied following Friday's USDA quarterly hog inventory report, which showed four percent less hogs as of December 1 than a year ago. The report also showed a surprising lack of hog herd rebuilding.
If pork prices get too strong it could keep retail interest focused on beef for advertising promotions, the market sources said.
